 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 3,50,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3849/2022 That on 20.03.2022 at about 11.00 to 11.10 a.m., when the Petitioner was travelling with other inmates in a Santro Car bearing Reg.No.KA03ML8328 on Malavalli town main road, in front of KSRTC bus stand, Court road, at that time, one Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's car and also further proceeded and hit against the another Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA09MF4093 and he lost control over the vehicle and hit against the road side electric pole.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner and inmates had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body and the Petitioner's car badly damaged.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Malavalli Government hospital and after first aid, he was referred to Vinodh Diagnosis and thereafter he visited to R.R. hospital,
wherein he admitted as an inpatient.

The SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3849/2022 Petitioner had spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working at Crazy Car Accessories Shop, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he lost his income and also unable to do his work.
He also spent Rs.71,550/ towards the Repair charges of his car for the damages occurred in the said accident.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11 C0926.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondents had appeared before the Court through their SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3849/2022 respective Counsels and filed Objection Statements to the main petition.

6. The Respondent No.1 has filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia denied the age,
avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that the Petitioner has not lodged any Complaint nor given any statement to the Police regarding accident, injuries and damages to the vehicle.

sentences.text: Further it contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 in his Objection Statement has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending goods vehicle.
Further, he denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and also the amount spent for the medical treatment of the Petitioner.
Further he stated that as on the date of alleged accident, the insurance Policy was in force and the driver also hold valid and effective Driving License.
Hence, the 1st Respondent who is the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, among these and other grounds the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

8. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
 SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3849/2022  ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 20.03.2022 at about 11.00 to 11.10 a.m., on Malavalli Town main road, in front of KSRTC bus stand, Court Road, Mandya due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 11C0926?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3.
What Order or Award?
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and closed his side evidence.
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3849/2022
On the other hand, the Respondents did not choose to lead any evidence.

10. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:

3 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

REASONS 11. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926 by its driver.
12.

On the other hand, both Respondents have denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3849/2022 offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926 by its driver.
13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P.1 to 7 are the FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, Seizer mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.17
are the Invoice, Medical bills, Prescriptions, Lab reports, X rays, Aadhaar card, RC and Copy of Policy with Certificate.

14. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P.1 and 2 are the True copies of the FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Mahadevaiah S/o Madaiah, the Malavalli Town Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926 for the offences punishable under Sec.
SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3849/2022 279 and 337 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P3 is the Spot mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the Seizer mahazar.
ExP5 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the offending vehicles.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner.

Ex.P7 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Malavalli Town Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.

15. Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P7 Column No.17 reads as under:

sentences.text: 16. P.W.1 has been crossexamined by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 and nothing could be elicited SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3849/2022 to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
It is to be noted here that in the Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6, the doctor has kept his opinion pending by stating that MLC extract from referral center required.
But, the said Wound Certificate shows that the Petitioner came to the said Government hospital, Malavalli with history of RTA, while going by car hit by Santro car.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, both Respondents did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence.
Hence, they failed to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C 0926 by its driver and due to the said accident, he had sustained injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
17. Issue No. 2: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3849/2022 driver of the offending goods vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18.
It is stated in the petition that, the Petitioner is aged 23 years at the time of accident.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhar card at Ex.P15, which shows his birth year was 1998.
The accident has taken place on 20.03.2022.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 24 years.
19. It is established that the Petitioner had suffered from injury in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Goods vehicle.
The Petitioner has contended that he had sustained injuries and he has spent huge amount for his medical treatment and other incidental charges.

The Petitioner has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P6 issued by the Malavalli Government Hospital, wherein it clearly mentioned that the Petitioner had sustained tenderness fracture left side of chest.
But, the doctor SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3849/2022 has kept opinion pending by stating that MLC Extract from referral center required.
20. The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor who issued the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P6.
The Petitioner has produced the Medical bills to prove expenditure towards medicines.
The bills at Ex.P9 would reveal that the Petitioner spent Rs.2,133/ towards medicines and other charges.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he spent huge amount towards treatment as contended in the petition.
21. Though the Petitioner has averred that he has become unable to do his work because of the injury sustained by him, no Physical Disability Certificate has been produced.
Further, he admitted in his evidence that he is working in the same shop and was getting salary of Rs.20,000/ p.m.
, The Petitioner has stated that he spent Rs.71,550/ for repairs for the damages SCCH 15 15 MVC Mohammed Saifulla vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd

The Petitioner has produced Invoice at Ex.P8.

But, in the crossexamination, PW.1 has admitted that he has not produced document for toying his car to the garage and he left his car after 15 - 20 days of the accident and he has not received Survey Report about the damages of his vehicle and he has not produced the document for leaving his vehicle in the garage and he has not produced the Receipt for payment of amount mentioned in Ex.P8.
It is pertinent to note here that he has not surveyed his vehicle and produced the Survey Report and not examined the person who issued Ex.P8.
Ex.P17 is the Copy of Policy which stands in the name of one Mr. Rajendra S. in respect of the car bearing Reg.No.KA03ML 8328.
Therefore, the Petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards the damages.

22. But, by considering the gravity of the injuries, pain and suffering, Medical expenses, food and nourishment and SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3849/2022 conveyance, it would be lawful to award global compensation of Rs.20,000/ to the Petitioner.

23. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11C0926.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
 SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3849/2022  ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.20,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, since the amount is meager,
the entire amount is ordered SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3849/2022 to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Mohammed Saifulla vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189680485/
6 Epayment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
